subject: geography
title: Water Stress & Scarcity
welcome_lead: Define stress, scarcity and virtual water.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on water stress, scarcity and Falkenmark indicator.

concepts.def: Insufficient natural supply; Middle East, parts of Africa.
Lack of infrastructure to access water; sub-Saharan Africa.
Water embodied in trade; UK imports ~50 percent of consumption indirectly.

walkthroughs.body_html: Falkenmark (1989) thresholds: 1700 m^3/capita = water stressed; 1000 m^3 = scarcity; 500 m^3 = absolute scarcity. UN Water 2022: 2.3 billion in water stressed countries; 733 million in high-stress (e.g. Egypt, Iran, Saudi Arabia). UK 1334 m^3/capita technically water stressed but with infrastructure capacity.

Physical scarcity in arid Middle East: Saudi Arabia 89 m^3/capita renewable; uses 30 percent of state energy on desalination. Economic scarcity in sub-Saharan Africa: rainfall available but infrastructure lacking; Ethiopia has rainfall but 65 percent of rural people lack piped water.

Tony Allan's concept: water in production. 1 kg beef = 15400 L water; 1 cup coffee = 140 L. UK imports 50-70 percent of water consumption embedded in food. Egypt imports 50 percent of grain (virtual water imports) because Nile insufficient for food self-sufficiency.
